title: Inductive reduction of positive bidual cohomology to complete normal constants
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $r\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$. Schemes below are Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use pinned potential dualizing complexes for dimension functions [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], the bounded constructible small etale category $D^b_c$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\eta_M:M\to D_K^2M$ for the transpose of evaluation after symmetry of the tensor factors. Fix $d\geq0$ and $q\geq1$. Assume that on all such schemes equipped with a dimension function, $D_K$ preserves $D^b_c$ and $\eta_M$ induces isomorphisms in degrees at most zero for every constructible sheaf $M$. Assume also: (i) $\eta_M$ is an isomorphism for every constructible sheaf on every such scheme of dimension less than $d$; (ii) for every such scheme $S$ of dimension at most $d$ and every constructible sheaf $M$, $\mathcal H^a(D_K^2M)=0$ for $1\leq a<q$. If $d\geq2$, assume in addition that $\mathcal H^q(D_K^2\Lambda_S)=0$ for every normal complete strictly henselian local such scheme $S$ of dimension exactly $d$, with every choice of dimension function and pinned potential complex. Then $\mathcal H^q(D_K^2M)=0$ for every constructible sheaf $M$ on every such scheme of dimension at most $d$. For $d=0$ or $d=1$ no additional constant-sheaf hypothesis is required. Complete means complete for the maximal-ideal adic topology; strictly henselian means henselian with separably closed residue field; normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. For a fixed scheme, changing its dimension function does not change these double-dual cohomology sheaves or the evaluation map, under their canonical identifications: two dimension functions differ by a locally constant integer $m$, and the corresponding potential complexes differ by the invertible twist-shift $K\mapsto K(m)[2m]$, which cancels in the double dual. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose XVII, 6.5, dimension-function independence following Definition 6.5.1; Lemmas 6.5.2–6.5.6 and the following reduction paragraph (normal local dimension at most one is regular; reduce dimension at least two by regular completion)

proof.text: Write $T_X(M)=\mathcal H^q(D_{K_X}^2M)$. The category of sheaves here is the ordinary small etale category. First verify dimension-function independence. On each irreducible component, two dimension functions have constant difference: follow a saturated chain from its generic point to a given point, and subtract the two dimension-function equalities at each immediate specialization. Differences agree on intersecting components, so on the finitely many components through a point they agree; after removing the other components this difference is constant on a neighbourhood. Thus it is locally constant. On a locus where the difference is $m$, tensoring the pinnings with $\Lambda(m)[2m]$ changes the costalk normalization to the new dimension function. Uniqueness [lem-per-potential-dualizing-uniqueness] identifies the new potential with this twist-shift. The Tate sheaf is an invertible line by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] (negative twists use its dual). Apply [lem-sf-etale-twisted-bidual-transport] with the identity morphism and $J=\Lambda(m)[2m]$. Its Hom comparisons are identities, and its conclusion identifies both double duals and their evaluation-transpose maps. These canonical comparisons agree on overlaps by pinning-preserving uniqueness.

For a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of constructible sheaves on a scheme of dimension at most $d$, [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], applied in the abelian category of etale $\Lambda$-module sheaves, gives a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ of the complexes concentrated in degree zero. Applying twice the contravariantly triangulated functor of [lem-per-relative-bidual-triangles] and then [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the cohomology exact sequence. If $q>1$, the term $\mathcal H^{q-1}(D^2C)$ is zero by the lower-degree induction hypothesis. If $q=1$, the preceding map $\mathcal H^0(D^2B)\to\mathcal H^0(D^2C)$ identifies with the epimorphism $B\to C$ by naturality of the assumed degree-zero isomorphisms. In both cases the connecting map into $T_X(A)$ is zero, and hence $0\to T_X(A)\to T_X(B)\to T_X(C)$ is exact. Therefore the class $T_X=0$ is closed under constructible subobjects and extensions. For a constructible subobject $A\subseteq B$ the quotient $C=B/A$ is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre](1), and in an extension of constructible $A$ and $C$ the middle term is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre](2); so hypothesis (ii) and the degree-zero assumption apply to all three terms. It is closed under finite sums and direct summands as well: the functor $D^2$ is additive, and inclusion and retraction remain inclusion and retraction after applying $T_X$.

source.place: XVII Lemma 6.5.2, including its separate q=1 argument

proof.text: For a finite map $p:Y\to X$ the comparison [lem-per-potential-finite-bidual-comparison] gives $p_*T_Y(N)\cong T_X(p_*N)$, and $p_*$ is exact and conservative. Here $K_Y=p^!K_X$ has the inherited potential pinnings, and both duality functors preserve bounded constructibility by the standing hypothesis. Thus vanishing is equivalent before and after finite pushforward. Schemes finite over an excellent Noetherian scheme are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; they remain Noetherian. They have dimension at most that of the target: on affine charts every strict chain of primes contracts strictly by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability]. Consequently all uses of step 2 on a finite source stay within the bound $d$.

It suffices to prove $T_Y(\Lambda_Y)=0$ for normal Noetherian excellent schemes $Y$ of dimension at most $d$, with any potential normalization. Indeed first treat constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaves as $\Lambda$-sheaves killed by $\ell$, without changing the duality coefficient ring. Their vanishing class is closed under extensions, finite sums and summands by step 2. By [lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation] it is enough to treat $p_*j_!\mathbf F_\ell$ for a finite $p:Y	o X$ with $Y$ integral and an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$. These generators are constructible: $j_!\mathbf F_\ell$ is lisse on the strata $U$ and $Y\setminus U$, and finite direct image preserves constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-fp-pushforward-constructible] (a finite morphism to a Noetherian scheme is of finite type, hence of finite presentation, and Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Let $
u:Y^
u	o Y$ be normalization. Its source is normal Noetherian excellent and $
u$ is finite surjective by [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation]; $
u_*\Lambda_{Y^
u}$ is constructible by the same pushforward lemma. The module injection $\mathbf F_\ell	o\Lambda$, $a\mapsto\ell^{r-1}a$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] give $j_!\mathbf F_\ell\hookrightarrow\Lambda_Y$. The finite comparison gives the monomorphism $\Lambda_Y\hookrightarrow
u_*\Lambda_{Y^
u}$. The proposed normal constant case, step 3, and closure under subobjects now give $T_Y(j_!\mathbf F_\ell)=0$, and step 3 gives the same for $p_*j_!\mathbf F_\ell$. Finally any constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $M$ has the finite filtration $M\supset\ell M\supset\cdots\supset\ell^rM=0$. Its factors $\ell^iM/\ell^{i+1}M$ are killed by $\ell$ and are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre](1), as images and cokernels of multiplication by powers of $\ell$. Extension closure proves the claim for $M$.

source.place: XVII Lemmas 6.5.4–6.5.5; XIII 3.7.2 for the existing integral-source generation node

proof.text: It remains to establish the normal constant case used in step 4. Test it on every strict localization $V=X_{(\bar x)}$. The regular comparison [lem-per-potential-regular-base-change] and the pinnings [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings] identify the pullback of the double dual and the evaluation map with those on $V$. The source is Noetherian excellent. The strict henselization of a normal local domain is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain]. Its dimension is $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq d$ by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension]. The local ring is the filtered etale colimit appearing in that normality statement. Thus $V$ is normal strictly local. If its dimension is less than $d$, hypothesis (i) already gives its biduality and therefore its positive cohomology vanishing. The strict-local tests detect vanishing: apply their stated isomorphism detection to $0\to T_X(\Lambda_X)$ regarded in degree zero; exact pullback commutes with $\mathcal H^q$. It therefore suffices to handle normal strictly local schemes of dimension exactly $d$.

source.place: XVII 6.5, etale locality paragraph and reduction following Lemma 6.5.5

proof.text: If $d=0$, the normal local domain is a field: its only prime is its zero ideal, so its maximal ideal is zero. If $d=1$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal] says it is regular local. In either case all localizations are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Choose the dimension function whose value at the generic point is zero. The constant sheaf has potential pinnings for it by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit], and any pinned potential for that function is isomorphic to it by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-uniqueness]. For $K=\Lambda$ the identities $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda,\Lambda)=\Lambda$ give $D_K^2\Lambda=\Lambda$, so its degree-$q$ cohomology is zero for $q\geq1$. Step 1 makes this independent of the initial dimension function. Thus neither of these dimensions needs an additional constant-sheaf hypothesis.

source.place: XVII 6.5, normal strictly local dimension at most one paragraph

proof.text: Now let $d\geq2$ and write the remaining strictly local normal scheme as $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Set $\widehat V=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$. The completion is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Its local ring and residue field are given by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. It is complete for its maximal ideal: [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied to $M=A$ gives completeness for $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, which is the maximal ideal by the local-ring statement. This application is valid since $A$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated; $(\mathfrak m\widehat A)^n=\mathfrak m^n\widehat A$. It is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], and its unchanged residue field is separably closed; thus it is strictly henselian. Its dimension equals $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension-eq]. Invertibility of $\ell$ is preserved by the ring map.

source.place: XVII 6.5, completion reduction immediately before Lemma 6.5.6

proof.text: The completion is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], using its Noetherian local completeness from step 7. To check normality, excellence of $A$ includes the G-ring condition. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] makes $A\to\widehat A$ flat with Noetherian geometrically regular fibres. Each fibre is regular by taking the trivial field extension, and hence normal by [rem-pc-regular-normal](1), applied to its spectrum. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] hold: both rings are Noetherian, the map is flat, its fibres are normal, and $A$ is normal. Therefore $\widehat A$ is normal. Since it is local, its localization at its maximal ideal is itself, so it is a normal domain by the definition of a normal ring. Together with step 7 this verifies every hypothesis of the additional constant-sheaf assumption for $\widehat V$.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent (2); Tag 0C23, lemma-completion-normal-local-ring and its cited Tag 0C22, algebra.tex lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian

proof.text: The completion morphism $h:\widehat V\to V$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular], since excellence includes the G-ring condition, and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Give $h^*K_V$ the potential pinnings of [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings]. Apply [lem-per-potential-regular-base-change] twice, to $\Lambda_V$ and to its bounded constructible dual. Exact pullback identifies $h^*T_V(\Lambda_V)$ with $T_{\widehat V}(\Lambda_{\widehat V})=0$, where the last equality is the additional hypothesis, now justified by steps 7–8. Apply [lem-etale-sheaf-jointly-surjective-conservative] to the singleton family consisting of $h$ and the sheaf map $0\to T_V(\Lambda_V)$; its inverse image is an isomorphism because its target is zero. Hence $T_V(\Lambda_V)=0$. Step 5 proves the normal constant case on all schemes of dimension at most $d$, and step 4 then proves $T_X(M)=0$ for every constructible $M$, as required.
